newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan CPC eyes solution for troubled Ecuador JV.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC eyes solution for troubled Ecuador JV.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum said a row over profits from an Ecuadoran oil-exploration project could end after imminent talks with venture partner and operator Maxus Energy Corp.

"A Maxus top executive will visit Taiwan to discuss a plan that would satisfy the Ecuadoran government's demand to share profits from the joint venture," oil monopoly vice president Hsieh Shih-hsiung told Reuters.
Company sources said Maxus' president would visit Taiwan in early October. Hsieh declined to discuss the visit in detail.

Ecuador in late August banned Maxus from operating a joint venture in the country's Block 16 oil field in the Amazon region. The government said the venture failed to share profits to the benefit of state oil firm Petroecuador.
Hsieh said exploration at the Ecuadoran oil field was still under way despite the government's decision.
Ecuadoran Energy and Mines Minister Alfredo Adum said on September 19 that a new deal with Maxus was ready for signing.
According to Adum, the Maxus-operated joint venture would have to "hand over to the Ecuadoran state 29 barrels of oil for every 100 barrels it produces".
Chinese Petroleum officials declined to comment on how Maxus' plan would share production with Ecuador.
As operator of the venture, Maxus holds 35 percent of its equity while Chinese Petroleum as the second-largest partner holds 31 percent.
Nomeco Ecuador Oil has 14 percent and Canam Offshore Ltd and Murphy Ecuador Oil Co each hold 10 percent, according to Chinese Petroleum documents.
